tier_rationale: Brother's own specification page lists Hi-Speed USB 2.0 as the sole interface and states the model lacks wireless and built-in Ethernet, while naming the wireless variants in the same series.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes. USB in, paper out. No radio, no account, no app, and nothing that can reach a Brother server. Predates the era when a printer expected a relationship with its manufacturer.

repairability.notes: TN630/TN660 toner and DR630 drum are separate units and still widely stocked years after discontinuation.

sources.supports: Manufacturer specification page: interface is Hi-Speed USB 2.0 only; model lacks built-in Ethernet and wireless, while HL-L2305W / HL-L2340DW / HL-L2360DW in the same series are listed with IEEE 802.11b/g/n.
Brother USA product page displays a 'Discontinued' status. Legacy list price $109.99.

open_questions: Secondhand price band not established — worth recording once a few completed sales are observed.
notes: Listed under 'discontinued but worth hunting'. Radio-free laser printers are getting rarer, so the secondhand market for these matters more than it would in most categories.
